fields.title: Adapting course advertising as learning preferences changed
fields.summary: MappedSkills has worked on AnybodyCanBake’s Meta advertising since 2018. When demand shifted back towards offline learning after COVID, approaches that had worked for online courses became less effective. Course price revisions and expansion into international markets helped the business return to profitability, according to MappedSkills founder Amit Gupta. For September 2021 to October 2026, the business reports 3,892 paid enrolments attributed to Facebook Ads and ₹2,78,95,678 in revenue on ₹42,78,961 in advertising spend.

content.value: What worked earlier stopped working as well

Amit describes a learning market that moved from offline towards online courses, swung back towards offline learning after COVID, and is now seeing renewed interest in online learning. For AnybodyCanBake, the shift back towards offline demand affected advertising economics and profitability.
Changing customer preference:
Selling an online learning offer became harder when more prospective learners preferred an offline experience.
Pressure on profitability:
Continuing with an approach that had worked earlier was no longer enough to maintain profitable acquisition.
The objective stayed the same:
The campaigns remained focused on sales. The response needed to address the commercial offer and the markets reached.
Revisit pricing and reach beyond the existing market

The response combined course price revisions with expansion of sales advertising into international locations. It addressed both the value of a sale and the markets in which the offer could find buyers.
Course price revisions:
Pricing was revised as part of the response to weaker advertising economics. Course names, prices and individual offers are not disclosed.
International expansion:
The advertising reach expanded into international locations, opening the offer to learners beyond the existing market.
Sales remained the focus:
The campaigns continued to pursue purchases through changing market conditions rather than changing the success measure to clicks or views.
3,892 paid enrolments and ₹2 crore 79 lakh in reported revenue
From September 2021 to October 2026, the reported totals show 3,892 paid enrolments attributed to Facebook Ads and ₹2,78,95,678 in revenue. The corresponding advertising spend was ₹42,78,961.
return on ad spend. Approximately ₹6.52 in reported revenue per ₹1 of advertising spend, calculated from the whole-period totals, September 2021 to October 2026.
paid enrolments attributed to Facebook Ads for the selected reporting period, September 2021 to October 2026.
in reported revenue, approximately ₹2.79 crore, across September 2021 to October 2026.
in advertising spend across September 2021 to October 2026.
advertising cost per paid enrolment. Advertising spend divided by paid enrolments, calculated from the whole-period totals.
A return to profitability with continued adaptation

Amit reports that price revisions and international expansion helped restore profitability. The engagement continues as online learning interest picks up again. These aggregate figures do not imply that results improved every month or that every phase was profitable.

fields.evidenceNote: The relationship history, market observations, sales-campaign objective, commercial changes and results were supplied by MappedSkills founder Amit Gupta. The displayed results cover September 2021 to October 2026, as supplied on 30 October 2026; they do not cover the full relationship since 2018 or a complete future month-end. Cost per enrolment is ₹42,78,961 divided by 3,892. ROAS is ₹2,78,95,678 divided by ₹42,78,961. These are whole-period calculations, not before-and-after comparisons. Phase-level results, attribution settings, refund treatment and a profit reconciliation were not supplied. The return to profitability is founder-reported; ROAS alone does not establish profit. The totals have not been independently checked against account exports and order records.

fields.title: Google Ads linked to 178 paid enrolments for a coaching institute
fields.summary: EKoching’s Google Ads engagement generated 4,124 enquiries and 178 attributed paid enrolments between August 2021 and September 2022. Reported revenue was ₹51,62,000 against ₹11,40,000 in advertising spend.

content.value: Measure the students who join as well as those who enquire

For a coaching institute, an enquiry starts a conversation; a paid enrolment is the commercial outcome. This case follows both stages so prospective education clients can assess the advertising cost against admissions.
Enquiries and admissions are different:
The campaign result needs to distinguish initial interest from a paid decision.
Follow the full journey:
Enquiries, admissions and revenue need to be read over the same reporting period.
Google Ads with admissions as the business measure

MappedSkills’ engagement covered Google Ads for EKoching. The supplied results connect enquiry generation with attributed paid enrolments and revenue, allowing the case to show both the response volume and the cost of an admission.
4,124 enquiries and 178 paid enrolments

The reported totals translate to ₹276.43 per enquiry and ₹6,404.49 in advertising spend per paid enrolment. Paid enrolments were equivalent to 4.32% of the enquiry count; this is a period-level ratio rather than a verified matched-cohort conversion rate.
attributed paid enrolments, August 2021 to September 2022.
return on ad spend. Reported revenue divided by advertising spend, calculated from the engagement totals, August 2021 to September 2022.
enquiries generated, August 2021 to September 2022.
advertising cost per paid enrolment. Advertising spend divided by attributed paid enrolments.
in advertising spend, August 2021 to September 2022.
in reported revenue, August 2021 to September 2022.

fields.evidenceNote: Figures and engagement dates supplied and confirmed by Amit Gupta on 30 October 2026. Cost per enquiry = ₹11,40,000 ÷ 4,124. Cost per enrolment = ₹11,40,000 ÷ 178. ROAS = ₹51,62,000 ÷ ₹11,40,000. Totals cover the engagement, not a before-and-after comparison. Attribution and refund treatment were not specified. Revenue return is not profit.

fields.title: Meta Ads linked to 3,957 products sold for Klenzmo
fields.summary: Klenzmo’s Meta Ads engagement recorded 3,957 products sold and ₹43,52,700 in reported revenue between September 2024 and March 2025, against ₹8,40,000 in advertising spend.

content.value: Connect product discovery with commercial results
For a specialist cleaning brand, advertising needs to move beyond attention to product sales. This case examines the reported product volume and revenue alongside the advertising investment.
Attention needs a buying outcome:
Reach and engagement alone do not explain the value of advertising to a product business.
Sales need a clear cost:
The number of products sold should be assessed against spend and reported revenue.
Meta advertising assessed against product sales

MappedSkills’ engagement covered Meta Ads for Klenzmo. The confirmed reporting scope is product sales, advertising spend and revenue during the selected period. Specific creative formats, audiences and optimisation decisions are not described until the delivery details are confirmed.
3,957 products sold and ₹43 lakh 53 thousand in revenue
The supplied totals produce an advertising cost of ₹212.28 per product sold and a 5.18× revenue return on advertising spend.
products sold, September 2024 to March 2025. Not labelled as orders, purchases or unique customers.
return on ad spend. Reported revenue divided by advertising spend, calculated from the reported totals, September 2024 to March 2025.
in advertising spend, September 2024 to March 2025.
in reported revenue, September 2024 to March 2025.
advertising cost per product sold. Advertising spend divided by products sold, calculated from the reported totals.

fields.evidenceNote: Figures and dates supplied and confirmed by Amit Gupta on 30 October 2026. Cost per product = ₹8,40,000 ÷ 3,957. ROAS = ₹43,52,700 ÷ ₹8,40,000. The count was supplied as products sold; it is not labelled as orders, purchases or unique customers. The figures do not establish profit, net revenue after refunds or new-customer acquisition cost.

fields.title: Google Ads linked to 4,324 products sold for Bakersville
fields.summary: Bakersville’s Google Ads engagement recorded 4,324 products sold and ₹47,56,400 in reported revenue between November 2025 and August 2026. Advertising spend for the period was ₹9,00,000.

content.value: Make product advertising accountable to sales

A baking-supplies business needs to assess whether advertising contributes to sales, not just website traffic. This case presents the reported sales volume and revenue against the advertising investment.
Traffic is only an intermediate result:
The useful business measures are products sold and the revenue attributed to the advertising.
Use a consistent reporting window:
Spend and sales outcomes need to cover the same period to make the comparison useful.
Google advertising with a product sales focus

MappedSkills’ engagement covered Google Ads for Bakersville. The confirmed outcome measures are products sold, advertising spend and revenue. The case does not specify Search, Shopping or Performance Max because the actual campaign formats have not yet been supplied.
4,324 products sold and ₹47 lakh 56 thousand in revenue
The reported totals produce ₹208.14 in advertising cost per product sold and a 5.28× revenue return on advertising spend.

fields.title: Google Ads linked to 640 new customers for Phoenix Laundry
fields.summary: Phoenix Laundry’s Google Ads engagement generated 1,600 enquiries and 640 new customers from December 2025 to 30 October 2026. Advertising spend was ₹4,00,000, with ₹7,68,000 in reported revenue.

content.value: Judge acquisition in the context of a repeat service

For a laundry business, a customer can return after the first transaction. The case therefore needs to show the acquisition cost and revenue already generated while keeping estimated lifetime value separate.
An enquiry is not a customer:
The enquiry count needs to be read alongside the number of new customers acquired.
Lifetime value needs context:
Expected future value can inform acquisition decisions, but it is not revenue already collected.
Google advertising measured through to new customers

MappedSkills’ engagement covered Google Ads for Phoenix Laundry. The supplied reporting follows the response from enquiries to new customers and reports revenue generated during the engagement. Specific services, locations and campaign changes remain to be confirmed.
640 new customers at ₹625 each in advertising spend

The reported new-customer count is equivalent to 40% of the enquiry count. Advertising cost was ₹250 per enquiry and ₹625 per new customer. Reported revenue was ₹7,68,000, equal to 1.92× advertising spend. The period-level ratio does not establish matched-cohort conversion.
new customers, December 2025 to 30 October 2026.
advertising cost per new customer. Advertising spend divided by new customers, calculated from the reported totals.
enquiries, December 2025 to 30 October 2026.
in advertising spend, December 2025 to 30 October 2026.
in reported revenue generated, December 2025 to 30 October 2026.
revenue return on ad spend. Reported revenue divided by advertising spend, calculated from the reported totals.
Customer lifetime value is a separate business estimate

The business supplied an average customer lifetime value of ₹50,000. It is an estimate with no method, horizon or revenue-versus-profit basis supplied. It is not realised revenue from these 640 customers and is not included in the revenue or ROAS figures above.

fields.evidenceNote: Figures, dates and average lifetime value supplied by Amit Gupta on 30 October 2026. Acquisition cost = ₹4,00,000 ÷ 640. ROAS = ₹7,68,000 ÷ ₹4,00,000. The ₹50,000 average lifetime value is a business estimate with no method, horizon or revenue-versus-profit basis supplied. It is not realised revenue from these 640 customers and is not included in ROAS.

fields.title: Meta Ads linked to 329 site visits and 23 reported sales for HutnHomes
fields.summary: HutnHomes’ Meta Ads engagement recorded 2,348 marketing-qualified leads, 845 sales-qualified leads, 329 site visits and 23 reported sales between September 2023 and December 2024. Advertising spend was ₹15,00,000 and reported revenue was ₹46,15,228.

content.value: Measure buyer progress beyond the first enquiry
Property advertising needs to be assessed through the sales journey. Qualified leads, site visits and reported sales provide a more commercially useful view than lead volume alone.
Qualification has stages:
Marketing-qualified and sales-qualified leads need separate counts and definitions.
Visits and sales matter:
The value of the lead flow becomes clearer when the case follows buyers towards site visits and sales.
Meta advertising with visibility into the sales journey

MappedSkills’ engagement covered Meta Ads for HutnHomes. The supplied results distinguish marketing-qualified leads, sales-qualified leads, site visits and reported sales. This gives the case a sales-journey view without assuming that platform lead submissions alone equal qualified buyers.
845 sales-qualified leads and 23 reported sales

Advertising cost worked out to ₹638.84 per marketing-qualified lead, ₹1,775.15 per sales-qualified lead and ₹4,559.27 per site visit. The spend per reported sale was ₹65,217.39. Reported revenue was 3.08 times advertising spend.
